us-house.budget-law-energy: a budget law that requires two offshore oil and gas lease sales a year through 2040, takes back public clean energy funds not yet spent, and ends tax credits both for electric vehicle purchases and for wind and solar plants whose construction starts after mid-2026 or whose operation starts after 2027. The official estimate valued the tax changes at about 0.17 percent of a year's economic output each year for ten years
us-house.vehicle-waiver-revocation: a resolution that became law and took away one regional government's power to require all new cars sold there to be zero-emission by 2035. Several other regional governments had adopted the same rule, and the regional government that set it expected it to cut carbon dioxide from cars there by about 395 million tons over 2026 to 2040, about 6 percent of one year's national emissions
us-house.methane-fee-repeal: a resolution that became law and scrapped the fee on oil and gas facilities' methane emissions beyond set limits; by the official estimate, the repeal costs about 0.002 percent of a year's economic output in revenue each year
us-house.review-limits-bill: a bill that passed the lower chamber but has not become law, confining national environmental reviews of projects to effects closely caused by them, putting deadlines on agency decisions, and reducing the window for a court challenge to a review from six years to 150 days; no official estimate says how many reviews it would cover

uk-commons.carbon-budget-order: a binding ceiling on the country's greenhouse gas emissions over 2038 to 2042, designed to reach a level 87 percent under that of 1990 by 2040; the government's assessment put its net investment cost at about 1.2 percent of a year's economic output each year
uk-commons.planning-infrastructure-law: a law speeding approval of large infrastructure such as power plants and grid lines and allowing builders to pay into a national nature fund rather than meet habitat protection duties at each site; the government expected about 150 decisions on major projects to come faster within the legislative term and put its value at about 0.1 percent of a year's economic output over ten years
uk-commons.nuclear-plant-decision: the government's final decision to go ahead with a new 3.2-gigawatt nuclear power plant, publicly funded at about 0.5 percent of a year's economic output, able to supply power equal to the needs of about 6 million homes

de-bundestag.climate-fund-amendment: a change to the constitution setting up a debt-financed infrastructure fund of about 11 percent of a year's economic output, spent across twelve years, that sends about 2.3 percent of a year's economic output to the fund for cutting emissions and adds net zero emissions by 2045 to the fund's purpose
de-bundestag.heating-law-rewrite: a law dropping the rule that new heating systems must use at least 65 percent renewable energy and permitting new oil and gas heating that burns a growing share of low-carbon fuel, rising from 10 percent in 2029 to 60 percent in 2040; the government said households save about 0.1 percent of a year's economic output a year and that it could not yet estimate the effect on emissions

fr-assemblee.energy-programming-bill: a bill laying down the national energy plan that the lower chamber rejected; it would have launched about 14 new nuclear reactors adding 27 gigawatts by 2050, about 43 percent above current nuclear capacity, and its amended text put a halt to every new wind and solar power project
fr-assemblee.low-emission-zones-repeal: a law, later struck down by the constitutional court, doing away with the zones in 25 urban areas in which older, more polluting vehicles may be kept out, of which the two largest had restrictions in force
fr-assemblee.farm-pesticide-law: a law allowing a banned insecticide of a class harmful to bees back into use, a provision struck down by the constitutional court, lifting the herd sizes at which livestock farms need fuller environmental permits, such as from 151 to 201 dairy cows, and treating new farm water reservoirs as presumed to be of major public interest

ca-commons.consumer-carbon-price-end: the removal of the carbon price on fuels that households and businesses buy, which the government expected to cost about 12.6 million tons of emission cuts over 2025 to 2031, about 1.8 percent of one year's national emissions
ca-commons.major-projects-law: a law under which the cabinet can name projects to be of national interest, treating them as approved under national laws on environmental assessment, fisheries, and species at risk on conditions it sets; in its first five months, the office it set up received projects worth about 4 percent of a year's economic output
ca-commons.regional-energy-accord: an agreement with one regional government that suspends clean electricity rules in that region and drops the planned cap on oil and gas emissions, which was to cut another 13.4 million tons by 2030 to 2032, about 2 percent of one year's national emissions, while the regional government lifts its carbon price on industry to an effective 130 per ton and backs a new oil export pipeline tied to carbon capture
